subject: general
question:
The volume (in cm³ ) of a wire of diameter 6 cm and length 56 m is:

Take pi = (22)/(7)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Radius (r)** = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 cm

**Height (h)** = 56 m = 5600 cm

**Volume** = πr²h = (22/7) × 3² × 5600

**Volume** = 22 × 9 × 800 = 1,58,400 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 1,58,400 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Diameter** of the wire = 6 cm

**Length (Height)** of the wire = 56 m

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a **Cylinder** = πr²h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e6fe5b1bc233c009a4ca4816f12745c19f50c8687a62cf3dbc68df02e3941ea1.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Radius (r)** = Diameter ÷ 2 = 6/2 = 3 cm

⇒ **Length (h)** = 56 × 100 = 5600 cm

⇒ **Volume** = (22/7) × 3 × 3 × 5600

⇒ **Volume** = (22/7) × 9 × 5600

⇒ **Volume** = 22 × 9 × 800

⇒ **Volume** = 198 × 800

⇒ **Volume** = 1,58,400 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 1,58,400 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of Cylinder

The amount of space occupied by a 3D cylindrical object is πr²h, where r is the radius and h is the height.

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

The area of the curved part of the cylinder is 2πrh.

Total Surface Area (TSA)

The sum of curved area and two circular bases: 2πr(h + r).

Unit Conversion

Always ensure all dimensions are in the same unit. 1 meter = 100 centimeters.</p
